en: A simple machine like a pulley reduces the effort force needed but does not decrease the total amount of work done.
Static friction prevents a parked jeepney from sliding down a steep hill even when the vehicle is completely stationary.
Gravity keeps the International Space Station in orbit around Earth, meaning astronauts experience microgravity rather than absolute zero gravity.
A strong neodymium magnet can attract nickel coins and cobalt alloys, proving magnets attract more than just pure iron.
A dry cell battery stores chemical energy and converts it into electrical energy only when connected to a complete circuit.
Light travels at a finite speed, taking approximately eight minutes to travel through space from the Sun to Earth.
Sound waves require a physical medium like air or water to travel, preventing any sound from traveling through empty space.
Thermal energy actually flows from a warm glass of juice into the ice cubes, rather than cold flowing out.
A rolling ball moving down a hill possesses both kinetic energy from its motion and gravitational potential energy from its height.
A third-class lever like a bamboo fishing pole increases the distance and speed of the load rather than reducing effort force.
Breaking a bar magnet in half creates two smaller magnets, each possessing its own distinct north and south magnetic pole.
Copper is a much better electrical conductor than iron, which is why copper is primarily used in household electrical wiring.
